sources: Batch instruction: install.md and upgrade.md name the round 2 candidate revision

confirmed: The startup log line 'migrations: reconciled 0090_onboarding_reviewed_types; continuing with pending migrations' is still correct from d1d098ba, because packages/db did not change.

compose.yml and Dockerfile did not change, so the app still runs migrations at boot, the worker still starts after the app, and OPENLAW_BUILD_COMMIT with the per-revision tags from install.md still builds without recreating running containers. Postgres stays postgres:16.

SMTP is now entered as discrete fields (server, port, security, authentication, sender). smtpSettingsToStorage writes the same encrypted smtpUrl and smtpFrom columns, the legacy smtpUrl/smtpFrom body is still accepted, and mailer.ts did not change. A relay saved on the starting build therefore still sends, and 'a test email through the saved relay' stays a valid check. Only the failure reason texts changed; the article does not quote them.

welcomeLoader still redirects to / when onboarding is completed, and apps/api/src/modules/onboarding did not change, so an upgraded instance is not sent back into the Welcome to OpenLaw wizard. The new shouldRevalidate rule only keeps the wizard on its URL step.

The sign-in screen now reads the public GET /api/v1/org/branding route and shows the organization name and logo. A failed branding request does not block sign-in. Step 2 'Sign in through the normal origin' needs no change.
The logo limit rose to 5 MB decoded. It changes no stored format; existing logos stay valid under the larger limit.

The .env.example and docs/DEPLOYMENT.md changes redefine BASE_URL as a browser-facing origin that can be private, and add a private VM overlay for new installs. The article already says to keep existing deployment settings unchanged, so it needs no new step.
The other commits change Settings list editing (explicit Save and Cancel), locked default Field display, and muted archived-user styles. They change no upgrade action or result.
docs/DEPLOYMENT.md still documents no supported downgrade. Restoring the pre-upgrade backup into a separate empty target with the old image stays the recovery path.
Prettier --check passes on the corrected article. Only the two revision strings changed.
